page: Vultr vx1-g-2c-8g-120s is a general-purpose virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core and 2 threads. The CPU operates at a base speed of 2.0 GHz and is equipped with 32 MB of L3 cache. The system is configured with 8.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core, and includes 120 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The server excels in single-threaded tasks, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression all ranking in the top 10% tier. Geekbench single-core and text processing scores are also strong, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance is limited, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and software compilation benchmarks falling into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth for large blocks and static web serving throughput remain average, while database operations and Redis SET performance are weak.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and high single-core efficiency, this server offers a balanced resource profile for workloads that do not require heavy parallelization. It is well-suited for lightweight single-threaded applications, basic web serving, text processing, and development environments. However, the low multi-core performance and weak database operation benchmarks suggest it is less optimal for heavy multi-threaded compilation, complex ray tracing, or high-throughput database hosting.
